headline: Anthropic's IPO filing shows $17bn a quarter and $895bn in compute bills, plus an aid-point massacre in Zaporizhzhia and Merz's pick for a female president

stories.title: Anthropic's amended IPO filing: $17bn Q3 revenue, a $23bn net loss and $895bn in compute commitments
facts: Anthropic filed an amended S-1 with the SEC on Monday, adding the third-quarter numbers its first filing left out.
Q3 revenue was about $16.96bn, up roughly 1,127% year on year; nine-month revenue reached $33.24bn versus $2.5bn a year earlier.
Q3 net loss was $23.29bn (down from $66.3bn in Q2), mostly from fair-value changes on convertible notes and derivatives; the operating loss was $567m after $974m operating income in Q2.
The company blames the operating loss mainly on $5.0bn of compute bought under pricier short-term commitments.
Total committed spend on compute and infrastructure is about $895.4bn; heise says nearly $450bn of that falls due before the end of 2030.

Growth is slowing quarter on quarter: about 47% in Q3 after 144% in Q2, per CNBC. Shares are planned for Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, and Reuters expects marketing to investors to start the week of Nov 9.
stories.whyItMatters: This is the clearest look yet at what frontier AI costs to run, weeks before what could be the biggest IPO on record.

stories.title: Russian bombs kill 18 at an aid point in Komyshuvakha as the Kherson truce ends
facts: At least nine 3,000 kg guided bombs hit the village in Zaporizhzhia region on Monday, regional head Mykhailo Semikin said.
18 people were killed, including a police officer and two rescuers; five were injured and 27 are missing.
Zelensky says a school used for weekly aid handouts was hit first, then the shelter where people took cover.
It came as the limited ceasefire that allowed the Oleshky evacuation expired and fighting resumed in Kherson region.
stories.whyItMatters: It ends the brief hope from the Oleshky truce that local pauses could lead to more.

stories.title: Merz wants a woman to succeed Steinmeier
facts: At a closed CDU meeting in Berlin, Merz said he will propose "a candidate of the political centre" and is set on it being a woman, according to participants cited by dpa, Reuters and FAZ.
The CSU wants Bavarian state parliament president Ilse Aigner and has backing from parts of the SPD and Greens; Merz insists the CDU has the right to nominate.
Names floated from the CDU include Julia Klöckner, Karin Prien, Annegret Kramp-Karrenbauer and Ines Claus.
A first decision could come at next Monday's CDU leadership meeting; the Federal Convention votes on Jan 30.
stories.whyItMatters: It rules out the men in the running and could give Germany its first female head of state.

stories.title: Midterms eve: DOJ goes to the Supreme Court over 20,000 California ballots, and a judge tosses the ex-FBI case as "weaponization"
facts: The Justice Department asked the Supreme Court to make California set aside mail ballots from about 20,000 people it calls likely noncitizens, after a district judge and a split 9th Circuit panel refused.
California calls the list unreliable; a UCLA analysis found 42% of the names aren't on the current voter roll and that the list includes naturalized citizens. The court has no deadline to act.
Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui dismissed the complaint against ex-FBI officials Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides, finding no probable cause and calling the case "weaponization" timed before the vote.
In Michigan, Democrat Abdul El-Sayed's campaign says it raised $2.4m on Sunday after his former primary rival endorsed the Republican.
stories.whyItMatters: Courts keep pushing back on federal moves around the vote, and the fights could carry on after Tuesday.

stories.title: OpenAI launches LifeVal, a benchmark for everyday tasks like booking, shopping and paperwork
facts: LifeVal measures how well models get practical things done, such as enrolling a child in kindergarten, ordering groceries or booking a car inspection.
Tasks were picked using US and international time-use studies plus a new survey of 3,995 people about where they want help.
OpenAI says GPT-6 Astra scores 100% on several tasks and that it has used the eval for a year to push browser use, computer use and connectors.
stories.whyItMatters: It shows where OpenAI is steering ChatGPT: from chatting toward an assistant that acts for you.

facts.text: The UK home secretary scrapped the plan to make migrant care workers already in the UK wait 15 years for permanent settlement.
A person in Yakima County, Washington, who caught bird flu from infected dairy cows has died.
Dutch police offer a record €2m reward in the hunt for a drug lord.
Zeit looks at Russian AI-made propaganda before the midterms, such as a fake Sarah Jessica Parker attacking Democrats.
Trump says he might pardon Elon Musk if Democrats win.
Space infrastructure startup Northwood Space raised $375m (Series C, a16z and DFJ Growth) at a $2bn valuation.
Nearly half of the games released on Steam in October disclosed AI-generated content, up from 1.7% in January 2024 (analysis of 63,600 games).
Former Xbox COO Helen Chiang denies the "policy violations" reportedly behind her firing.
Business Insider reports that Anthropic's internal AI use, priced at retail, now exceeds what it pays its employees.

facts.text: Vercel MCP now shows deployments as an interactive card, so you can monitor them inside ChatGPT.
Vercel Sandbox with Drives starts up to 2.4x faster; Vercel Flags can now be evaluated from another project without sharing SDK keys, and Flags Explorer was redesigned for sharing overrides.
Google announced a Quick Share SDK for Android and iOS for the first half of 2027, so apps can embed peer-to-peer sharing and Tap to Share.
From today, Firebase AI Logic requires App Check enforcement, so set up attestation providers or the generative features stop working.
OpenRouter says it now handles 100 trillion tokens a week; going from 10T to 100T took 28 weeks.
Dax (thdxr) warns that GitHub org and repo secrets can be stolen by anyone with write access who gets hacked; put secrets in environments with protection rules.
Merged: SvelteKit's adapter-vercel now accepts every Node.js version from 26 up, and TypeScript fixed an exponential base-type search in hasBaseType.
